purpose: Non-admission original-provider discovery of six Germany/England/Europe flood-depth, radar-hail and regional climate-risk research products; no source bytes, data admission, model approval or publication permission.

entries.name: Germany HWRM-RL cycle 3 harmonised river and coastal flood-depth classes
entries.provider: Bundesanstalt fuer Gewaesserkunde (BfG) / WasserBLIcK / German federal and state water authorities
entries.spatial_scope: Germany; national harmonised reporting coverage, regional higher-resolution original layers may differ
entries.temporal_scope: EU Floods Directive HWRM-RL third cycle 2022-2027; GovData publication 2026-03-06, reporting snapshot not an annual event chronology
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Flood-depth polygon classes 0-0.5, 0.5-1, 1-2, 2-4 and over 4 metres; low/medium/high probability and river/coastal scenarios; T_class combines area type with depth class
entries.note: Official GovData page describes HWRM third-cycle reporting, probability classes and depth-band T_class encoding (for example 23 indicates the informational flood area and 1-2 m depth). This is a nationally harmonised static scenario product; it is not a gauge-observed historic event, individual-property water depth, annual occurrence model, insured loss, or proof of local completeness. Verify the original BfG service endpoints, CRS, source authority, exact source vintage, provider-specific terms and state-level alternatives before access or commercial model use. Publisher metadata defines river/inland depth relative to the watercourse bed and coastal depth relative to seabed/chart datum and tide; this is not independently validated inundation above building ground elevation. Area-type digit 3 of T_class is a flood-protected area, not evidence of a flooded insured building. Do not translate these classes directly into building-depth loss without original service schema, terrain reference and spatial support verification.

entries.name: England Environment Agency rivers and sea defended and undefended flood depths present day
entries.provider: UK Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
entries.spatial_scope: England; only areas with national flood-zone modelling, with explicit Unavailable attribute elsewhere
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Seven depth bands up to and over 2300 mm; defended and undefended 0.1% AEP; river 1% AEP and sea 0.5% AEP; OGC API Features, WFS, WMS and GeoJSON/Geodatabase ZIP links listed
entries.note: Publisher lists Open Government Licence, EPSG:27700 and explicit Unavailable regions. Defended assumes flood defences perform as designed; no defence-failure scenario. Depths are categorical scenario estimates, not exact depth at an individual insured building or event observations. Confirm the exact 2026 revised asset/OGC layer URL, request limits, geographic completeness, attribution and commercial automation before download or modelling. Never coerce Unavailable to zero depth.

entries.name: England Environment Agency rivers and sea flood-depth climate-change scenarios
entries.provider: UK Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
entries.spatial_scope: England; national flood-zone modelling supported polygons, local depth may be Unavailable
entries.temporal_scope: Climate-change scenario dataset updated 2026-10-30; river 2080s epoch 2070-2125 and coastal sea-level-rise allowance to 2125
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Seven depth bands in defended/undefended 0.1% AEP and river 1% / sea 0.5% AEP cases; UKCP18 RCP8.5 allowances
entries.note: Official climate-change product is scenario-conditioned, not observed annual losses and not a current-baseline flood-frequency distribution. River central allowance for the 2080s and coastal upper-end allowance to 2125 use UKCP18/RCP8.5; defences assumed to function unchanged. Preserve scenario, epoch, exceedance definition, Unavailable cells, and shared lineage with the corresponding present-day product; these two products are not independent observed evidence.

entries.name: England Environment Agency surface-water spatial-planning flood-depth classes present day
entries.provider: UK Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
entries.spatial_scope: England, within coverage and planning-product limitations
entries.temporal_scope: Present-day planning scenario product published 2026-05-28, catalogue updated 2026-07-06
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Depth bands up to 150 mm, 150-300, 300-600, 600-900, 900-1200, 1200-2300 and over 2300 mm; 3.3%, 1% and 0.1% AEP scenarios; WMS and download links
entries.note: A separate pluvial/surface-water source, not a replacement for fluvial/coastal depth mapping. The Environment Agency explicitly says planning depth bands are not suitable for determining whether an individual property floods. Retain AEP, spatial support, depth bins, release and lineage; avoid counting overlap with river/sea flooding as independent losses. Review service access and original product licence for automated commercial use.

entries.name: DWD single-radar PZ volume reflectivity data for historical hail-cell research
entries.provider: Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD); 2026 analysis by KIT and CEDIM (Mohr et al.)
entries.spatial_scope: German DWD radar stations; individual station footprints may cross national borders
entries.temporal_scope: DWD directory observed 2026-11; 2026 paper analyses summer seasons 2005-2024 using archived PZ volumes, but public directory's exact historical availability is not yet established
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Per-station 3D radar reflectivity PZ files, 12 altitude layers and six reflectivity classes in the study; original study uses a homogeneous 15-minute composite for 2005-2024
entries.note: The original station directory contains PZ radar files and station folders; the 2026 peer-reviewed publication https://doi.org/10.3389/fenvs.2026.1736782 reports 15,577 potential hail tracks for 2005-2024, not a publicly verified separately downloadable PHT dataset. Reflectivity indicates potential hail cells, not confirmed hailstone size, individual insured property loss or independent claims. Historical file retention, polarimetric/version changes, outage coverage, machine access, exact DWD weather-radar terms and licence need source-specific verification. Do not extend CDC-specific CC BY terms to this weather-radar product without review.

entries.name: JRC TRACE / PESETA V pan-European regional climate-risk and economic-impact scenarios
entries.provider: European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC) / Disaster Risk Management Knowledge Centre
entries.spatial_scope: European regions covered by JRC TRACE / PESETA V regional dashboard
entries.temporal_scope: Dashboard announced 2026-10-30; regional modelled impacts across global warming levels and socioeconomic scenarios
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Regional economic impact and exposure scenario tables by risk, geography and warming level; underlying table reported downloadable from dashboard
entries.note: JRC official 2026-10-30 announcement https://joint-research-centre.ec.europa.eu/jrc-news-and-updates/jrc-makes-climate-risk-data-europes-regions-available-through-single-dashboard-2026-10-30_en describes region/hazard/warming-level comparability and downloadable dashboard tables. These are modelled economic damages/exposures, not independent insurer claims or catastrophe event losses; preserve inflation base year, scenario, spatial aggregation, hazard models and common upstream assumptions. Risk Data Hub API portal documents EU Login/API-token requirements; do not assume that dashboard tables are available through an anonymous API, or that the API licence covers every table. Obtain exact table receipt and publication terms separately.
